answer: A hardware attestation protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to bind identities to certified secure enclaves. An attacker incurs the verifiable expense of purchasing scarce physical silicon per identity, driving adversary margins to a nadir. Whether verifying a state delta or routing a pearl trade, an agent must present valid cryptographic signatures. However, this mechanism enforces supply-chain centralization and remains vulnerable to hardware side-channel exploits.
